==English== ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*seh₁-|id=sow}} From {{inh|en|enm|ernen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|earnian}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*aʀanōn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*azanōną}}. This verb is denominal from the noun {{m|gem-pro|*azaniz|t=harvest}}. ====Pronunciation==== * {{enPR|ûrn|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/ɜːn/}} * {{enPR|ûrn|a=US}}, {{IPA|en|/ɝn/}} * {{IPA|en|/ɛːrn/|/ɛrn/|a=Early Modern}}{{R:en:Dobson:1957|II|8|472|passage=''Earn'' is recorded with ''ĕ'' by Levins (against ''ę̄''), Hodges, Poole, Coles, Stringer, Brown, and the ‘homophone’ lists from Wharton onwards; with ''ę̄'' by Levins (beside ''ĕ''), Price, and Cooper (followed by Aickin).}} * {{audio|en|en-us-earn.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|ɜː(ɹ)n|s=1}} * {{homophones|en|ern|erne|urn}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb|+|+|+,~t}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[gain]] ([[success]], reward, recognition) through applied [[effort]] or [[work]]. #: {{ux|en|You can have the s'mores: you '''earned''' them, clearing the walkway of snow so well.}} #: {{ux|en|With their hard work and dedication, they '''earned''' respect and a seat at the table.}} #* {{RQ:Hough Purchase Price|chapter=II|text=Carried somehow, somewhither, for some reason, on these surging floods, were these travelers, of errand not wholly obvious to their fellows, yet of such sort as to call into query alike the nature of their errand and their own relations. It is easily '''earned''' repetition to state that Josephine St. Auban's was a presence not to be concealed.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=November 12, 2011|work=BBC Sport |title=[http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/15693231.stm International friendly: England 1-0 Spain] |passage=England will not be catapulted among the favourites for Euro 2012 as a result of this win, but no victory against Spain is '''earned''' easily and it is right they take great heart from their efforts as they now prepare to play Sweden at Wembley on Tuesday.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[receive]] payment for work or for a role or position held {{ng|(regardless of whether effort was applied or whether the [[remuneration]] is [[deserved]] or [[commensurate]])}}. #: {{ux|en|He '''earns''' seven million dollars a year as CEO.  My bank account is only '''earning''' one percent interest.}} #: {{ux|en|She '''earns''' more than forty thousand dollars a year in passive income from her parents' investments — that's what she gets before she even gets out of bed or lifts a finger.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To receive payment for work. #: {{ux|en|Now that you are '''earning''', you can start paying me rent.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause (someone) to receive payment or reward. #: {{ux|en|My CD '''earns''' me six percent!}} #: {{ux|en|In that era, all their long, hard, dangerous labor in the mines barely '''earned''' them even enough to eat!}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To achieve by being worthy of. #: {{ux|en|to '''earn''' a spot in the top 20}} =====Usage notes===== The verb has senses of "get because deserving" and "get whether deserving or not", but because to many ears it [[Appendix:Glossary#connotation|connotes]] the former meaning, writers and speakers sometimes resist using it for the latter meaning, choosing instead synonyms such as ''[[get#Verb|get]]'', ''[[take in#Verb|take in]]'', or ''[[rake in#Verb|rake in]]''. =====Conjugation===== {{en-conj|old=1|past2=earnt}} =====Synonyms===== * {{sense|gain through applied effort or work}} {{l|en|deserve}}, {{l|en|merit}}, {{l|en|garner}}, {{l|en|win}} * {{sense|(transitive) receive payment for work}} {{l|en|get}}, {{l|en|take in}}, {{l|en|rake in}} * {{sense|(intransitive) receive payment for work}} {{l|en|rake it in}} * {{sense|cause someone to receive payment or reward}} {{l|en|yield}}, {{l|en|make}}, {{l|en|generate}}, {{l|en|render}} =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|hard-earned|unearned|earnings|nonearning|unearning|earner|earnings|earn one's keep|earn out|earnout|unearned|overearn|underearn|outourn|earn a living|earn one's corn|earn one's crust|earn one's spurs|earn one's stripes|earn one's wings| earn a crust|pay as you Spanish: * Thai: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|cause someone to receive money}} * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 2=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃er-}} Probably either:{{R:OED Online|pos=''v.''{{sup|3}}|noformat=1|id=58996|date=December 2020}} * from {{inh|en|enm|erne}}, {{m|enm|ernen|t=to coagulate, congeal}} {{qualifier|chiefly South Midlands}} {{nb...|(chiefly Middle English from Southwest England and Southwest Midlands, and Early Middle English) eorne, eornen, herne, hurnen, uerne, urne, urnen, hurnen, (Early Middle English, Southwest Midlands) eærne, earnæ, heorne, hirnen, irne, irnen|otherforms=1}}, a {{glossary|metathetic}} variant of {{m|enm|rennen|t=to run; to coagulate, congeal}}, from {{inh|en|ang|rinnan|t=to run}} (with the variants {{m|ang|iernan}}, {{m|ang|irnan}}) and {{der|en|non|rinna|t=to move quickly, run; of liquid: to flow, run; to melt}},{{R:MED Online|entry=rennen|pos=''v.''(1)|noformat=1|id=MED36797}} both from {{der|en|gem-pro|*rinnaną}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₃er-|t=to move, stir; to rise, spring}}; or * a {{back-formation|en|earning|t=(''Britain regional, archaic'') rennet|nocap=1}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} {{tlb|en|Britain|dialectal}} # {{lb|en|transitive|archaic}} To [[curdle]] ([[milk#Noun|milk]]), especially in the [[cheesemaking]] [[process#Noun|process]]. #: {{synonyms|en|run|yearn|q2=Northern England, Scotland}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} Of milk: to curdle, especially in the cheesemaking process. ===Etymology 3=== A variant of {{m|en|yearn}}.{{R:OED Online|entry=† earn|pos=''v.''{{sup|2}}|noformat=1|id=58997|date=December 2020}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[strongly]] [[long#Verb|long]] or [[yearn#Verb|yearn]] (for something or to [[do#Verb|do]] something).{{R:Webster 1913}} #* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|canto=I|book=I|stanza=3|passage=And ever as he rode, his hart did '''earne''' / To prove his puissance in battell brave.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[grieve]].{{R:Webster 1913}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 5|act=II|scene=iii|page=75|column=2|passage=[M]y manly heart doth '''erne'''. {{...}} Boy, [[bristle|briſsle]] thy Courage vp: For ''[[w:John Falstaff|Falſtaffe]]'' hee is dead, and wee muſt '''erne''' therefore.}} ===Etymology 4=== ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{alternative form of|en|erne}}{{R:Webster 1913}} #* {{RQ:Scott Lay of the Last Minstrel|passage=They gleamed on many a dusky tarn ,
Haunted by the lonely '''earn''' }} ===References=== {{reflist}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=aenr|nare|rean|Near|eRNA|Rane|near|Arne|Nera|erna}}

==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|learnyng||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|lernyng}}, {{m|enm|lernynge}}, from {{inh|en|ang|leornung|t=learning, study}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*liʀnungu|t=learning}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|learn|-ing|id2=gerund noun}}. Cognate with {{cog|osx|lernunga}}, {{cog|de|Lernung}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈlɝnɪŋ/|a=GA}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈlɜːnɪŋ/|a=RP}}
* {{hyphenation|en|learn|ing}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-learning.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɜː(ɹ)nɪŋ|s=2}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|-|s}}

# {{lb|en|uncountable}} An act in which something is [[learn]]ed.
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} Accumulated [[knowledge]].
#: {{ux|en|The department head was also a scholar of great '''learning'''.}}
# {{lb|en|countable|proscribed}} Something that has been learned.
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=April 5, 2007|author=Stuart Elliott|title=Online Experiment for Print Magazine|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2007/04/05/business/media/05adco.html
|passage=“We’ll take the '''learnings''' and apply them to the rest of our business.”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251014084345/https://www.nytimes.com/2007/04/05/business/media/05adco.html|archivedate=14 October 2025}}

====Usage notes====
* Countable sense “thing learned” often used in plural form {{m|en|learnings}}; see [[learnings#Usage notes|''learnings:'' Usage notes]] for details.
